messages.subject: boostrapLavaan returning error and stopping
parts:
Hi all--
I am attempting to fit a 3-factor CFA model with 47 observed categorical variables using the non-parametric bootstrap function. Though I am able to directly estimate the model, running 100 bootstrap replications will sometimes return an error indicating "computational singularity" and discontinue the procedure without compiling the results. The error:

Error in solve.default(A1) : 
  system is computationally singular: reciprocal condition number = 7.03739e-31

Is it possible to set the "warn" option to pass by these instances instead of failing and quitting?

My data header, model, and bootstrap commands are included below.

Thanks for any insight!

--Matthew

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: boostrapLavaan returning error and stopping
parts:
running 100 bootstrap replications will sometimes return an error indicating ...


Hi Matthew,

The data you provided appears only to be the top 6 rows of your data.  How many observations do you have, and do you have any small marginal proportions?  Because you only get the error "sometimes", I wonder whether some bootstrap samples return a variable with no variance (i.e., all sampled observations are from the same category) or variables that appear redundant/multicollinear.

If this is the problem, you might get around the problem by bootstrapping yourself, and include a check of each bootstrap sample before trying to analyze it, until you return results from as many bootstrap replications as you want.  However, I don't know the behavior of bootstrap CIs if they are calculated conditional on certain samples like this.
